name: Ansible plaintext connection credentials
attack_scenario: the plaintext password is exposed to anyone with repo read access, in CI logs, or in `ansible-playbook -vvv` output, and is reused by an attacker to log in or escalate on the managed hosts
negative_test_hint: set ansible_ssh_pass to "PlaintextP@ssw0rd!" in a playbook and assert it is flagged and replaced with a vault reference or key-based auth

exemplar.explanation: Hardcoding ansible_ssh_pass / ansible_become_password / url_password (etc.) as a literal puts the credential in plaintext in the repo and in verbose -vvv logs, where anyone with read access can reuse it to log in or escalate on the managed hosts. Ansible Vault, a {{ }} template lookup, or key-based authentication keeps the secret out of the playbook entirely.
